turns.human_input: Given the school district factor for our 12-year-old specifically — is that enough to tip the decision toward moving even with the higher payment?

Yes, for the 12-year-old specifically, it tips toward moving. If you genuinely believe the Sellwood or Lake Oswego schools are materially better — not just marginally — that's a time-sensitive window you can't recover. You can refinance a mortgage when rates drop; you can't redo your kid's 8th-10th grade years.

The payment gap (~$1,700-1,900/month more to move) is real and significant, but it's not insurmountable on two incomes if you're otherwise financially stable. The honest answer: if the school district difference is what you and your spouse actually believe it is, move. Don't renovate a house in a neighborhood you've decided to leave — that's throwing good money at the wrong problem.
